6. Components

Each part has one rule. The rule decides; the examples only illustrate it. Every class here is in css/base.css, and specimens/foundations.html shows each one in its states. This is the look of a part and when to use it, not an API: a product that builds on a framework, such as Material UI, draws the same parts with its own components (Applying it).

Keys and Wells

A key is anything pressed; a well is anything filled. Classes .key and .well.

  • Rule. A key stands 2 pixels proud on a hard lip and travels down when pressed. A chosen key stays down with its lamp lit: it is latched. A well is cut in, with a shade under its top edge.
  • Do. Use one primary key in a view, .key--primary. Use a ghost key, .key--ghost, for an action that repeats in every row. Put a field's label above its well, in sentence case.
  • Don't. Don't add a gradient, a glow or a blurred shadow. Don't float a label inside a well. Don't raise something that cannot be pressed.

A set of latching keys is tabs: one is down. A check box, a radio and a slide switch are the same family: a radio is a lamp in a ring, and a switch shows an I or an O as well as its position, so its state never rests on color.

Lamps

A small light beside a word. Classes .lamp, .status and .chip.

  • Rule. State is a lamp and a word together. Lit and filled is on; a hollow ring is off; a triangle warns; an octagon stops.
  • Do. Change the shape with the state, so the state survives without color.
  • Don't. Don't show a lamp without its word. Don't use a lamp as decoration or as a bullet.

Screens

A deep field of the secondary hue with lit type on it. Class .screen, and .readout for one value.

  • Rule. What the system reports is shown on a screen: code, commands, counts, a document, a secret. A screen is the same in both themes.
  • Do. Light a line to point at it. Keep amber, --nc-color-screen-hot, for literals and for sensitive values.
  • Don't. Don't put running text or a form on a screen. Don't color syntax in more than the one hue and amber.

Engraved Names, Displayed Values

Two type voices. Classes .label and .value.

  • Rule. A fixed part of the case is named in narrow capitals: a column head, a group head, a tag, the kind of a boundary. A value the system reports is monospace. Everything a person reads as a sentence is sentence case.
  • Do. Set the label of a field in sentence case, and show the key a setting is stored under beside it as a value.
  • Don't. Don't engrave a sentence, a caption or a field label. Don't set prose in monospace.

The Boundary Plate

The kind and the name of a security boundary between the mark's own braces, on a lit plate. Class .boundary.

  • Rule. The plate names Platform, Team or Tenant, and nothing else. It appears on the display, and again in every dialog that acts inside the boundary.
  • Do. Give each kind its icon, its word and its fill: a tenant is lit in the tenant's color, a team is white, the platform is amber with tape at its edge.
  • Don't. Don't use it as a tag, a badge or a status. Don't change its words. Don't show a kind by color alone.

The Display

One dark screen in the console's bar. Class .display.

  • Rule. The display holds state and never a control: the three boundaries in order with the active one lit, the page, and who is signed in.
  • Do. Keep it in view. The bar is sticky, so the boundary is on screen at every scroll position and on a phone.
  • Don't. Don't put a key, a link or a field on it. Don't add a second display to a page.

Hazard Tape

Classes .hazard and .alert--warning. Tape means "this is not routine": Shape, depth and the brace has its rule.

The Rest of the Kit

PartClassesUse it for
Plate.plate, .plate--raisedA flush panel on the case; raised, it stands as proud as a key: a sign-in card
Alert.alert, the info alert; .alert--success, --warning and --dangerA message with a signal bar, an icon and a word; a caution wears tape
Chip and tag.chip, .tagA status as a lamp and a word; an engraved name with an edge
Table.tableRows of values: an engraved head on a sunken ground, values in the value voice
Selector.navkeyA column of names with one latched, its lamp lit
Dialog.dialogAn overlay that restates its boundary with the plate beside its title; a sheet on a phone
Tooltip.tooltipA small screen: the screen's field and its ink
